title: A Comparative Study of Semantic Similarity Measures for AI-Based Resume-Job Matching: Evidence from Public Recruitment Datasets
content: The rapid adoption of Artificial Intelligence (AI) in recruitment has significantly transformed the process of matching job seekers with employment opportunities. Traditional keyword-based resume screening methods often fail to capture the semantic relationships between candidate qualifications and job requirements, resulting in inaccurate ranking and reduced recruitment efficiency. Recent advances in Natural Language Processing (NLP) and semantic representation learning have introduced sophisticated similarity measures capable of understanding contextual meanings beyond exact keyword matching. This study presents a comparative analysis of widely used semantic similarity techniques for AI-based resume-job matching using publicly available recruitment datasets. Specifically, the research evaluates traditional lexical approaches, including TF-IDF with Cosine Similarity and Jaccard Similarity, alongside modern contextual embedding methods such as BERT, Sentence-BERT (SBERT), and BERTScore. A qualitative secondary-data research methodology is adopted by synthesizing findings from peer-reviewed studies, benchmark datasets, and open-source recruitment repositories. The comparison focuses on semantic understanding, computational efficiency, robustness, scalability, interpretability, and suitability for real-world recruitment applications. The findings indicate that transformer-based embedding models consistently outperform conventional lexical methods in identifying semantically relevant candidate-job relationships, particularly when resumes and job descriptions use different vocabulary to describe similar competencies. The study contributes a comprehensive comparative framework that assists researchers, HR professionals, and system developers in selecting appropriate semantic similarity measures for intelligent recruitment systems while highlighting current research challenges and future directions in explainable and fair AI-driven hiring.
